title: Trusting 72-hour amyloid or complement-only antibody checks, pooling coating washout with natural decay, scaling 70:20:10 loading from assumed cell ratios, or splicing unverified BRICHOS fusions
idea: Clear chronically stressed grafts on a single 72-hour amyloid stain, clear sensitised recipients on complement lysis without Fc-receptor killer cells, pool fast washout and natural coating decay or count retained SA-FHL-1 as complete depletion, cut cell loading by 14.3% from a nominal 70:20:10 label without measuring beta-cell output, or splice chimeric INS/PCSK1/Bri2 BRICHOS constructs into active safe-harbour payloads.
why: Amyloid toxicity in stem-cell and encapsulated islets builds over weeks rather than 72 hours, and non-complement IgG1/IgG3 antibodies can still trigger CD16+ natural-killer ADCC even when complement is quiet—while subtracting high depleted-serum background could hide 30% total killing behind a 1% net difference. Pooling fast washout with aged coatings blurs distinct rebound risks, a 5% drop in per-beta output raises equal-dose oxygen demand past the 0.90 ceiling, and oversized or furin-cleaved Bri2 chimeras exceed the 2,755-bp AAVS1 donor cap or release secreted C-terminal fragments.
check: Cap both intact-serum killing and IgG-attributable CD16+ ADCC increment at or below 5.0% against FcγRIIIa-158V/V effectors, segregate Arm 2 washout, natural decay and parallel active Arm 3 controls without cross-arm batch borrowing, scale 70:20:10 loading by measured starting per-beta output while holding both insulin and glucagon AUC ratios at or above 0.85, and require concordant 72-hour, Day-28 and Day-84 oligomer ELISA plus colocalized fibril imaging across at least 6 lots alongside viable beta mass.
instead: Enforce paired intact-plus-increment CD16+ ADCC and segregated post-depletion Gate 0d checks, gate 70:20:10 loading on measured output and dual-band worst-face oxygen, and hold native ITM2B (NM_021999.5) at 0% active weight unless concordant chronic amyloid breach is confirmed.

title: Inserting protective genes into the insulin (INS) 3′-UTR via an EIF4G2 leader, leaving half the graft unshielded and stretching insulin mRNA 37-fold
idea: Drop a bicistronic EIF4G2-driven protective cassette into the 73-nucleotide 3′-UTR of the insulin gene (INS) on chromosome 11p15.5 so beta cells express immune shields without touching another locus.
why: Nearly half (48.6%) of the cells in a curative graft—alpha, delta, blood-vessel and support cells—do not transcribe INS at all and would be left unshielded. Cutting the 73-nucleotide INS 3′-UTR hits the pyrimidine-rich stability element (ins-PRS) on 8 of 15 Cas9 guides, stretching the 3′-UTR 37-fold to 2,711 nucleotides invites Upf1-mediated mRNA decay, human EIF4G2 leader fragments carry cryptic promoter and upstream start-codon risks, and double-strand breaks at 11p15.5 sit 1.2 kb from imprinted IGF2.
check: Keep protective transgenes at constitutive or inflammation-responsive safe-harbour loci expressed across every graft cell type, and verify intact INS mRNA stability and 11p15.5 allelic balance (BAF within 0.45 to 0.55) if any point edit touches INS.
instead: Retire INS 3′-UTR EIF4G2 knock-ins permanently (settling the knock-in half of OQ-011) and stage Design B’s 2A-free protective genes at CXCL10 and divergent AAVS1 on research hold while keeping scored B1’s separate INS signal-peptide hypothesis distinct.

title: Screening guides on reference DNA alone, cutting HLA-A and HLA-B in one pass, reading DT9 staining without an HLA-E control, or skipping mismatch-repair checks on PE4max
idea: Rely on one reference genome or fixed allele cut-offs for guide off-targets, edit HLA-A and HLA-B simultaneously without checking all HLA-C alleles, read DT9 antibody staining directly as proof of retained HLA-C, or switch TYK2 prime editing to mismatch-repair-inhibited PE4max without microsatellite-instability gates.
why: Donor variants can create or disrupt CRISPR cut sites missed on GRCh38, simultaneous HLA-A and HLA-B cuts can delete the 1.41 Mb interval holding HLA-E and retained HLA-C, antibody clone DT9 cross-reacts with HLA-E (so HLA-E+ / HLA-C-null cells still stain positive), whole-genome B-allele averages hide balanced reciprocal chromosome losses across edited arms, and transient MLH1 inhibition in PE4max can leave genome-wide repeat indels if unchecked.
check: Join target variants by normalized coordinates against gnomAD v4.1 plus 30x donor WGS, screen HLA-A/B guides across phased donor HLA-A/B/C/E alleles in separated passes with per-locus phased BAF in [0.45, 0.55], include a matched HLA-E-only (HLA-C-null) specificity control beside DT9 + 3D12, and gate held PE4max on zero microsatellite shifts and a clonal repeat-indel cap.
instead: Enforce variant-aware gnomAD v4.1 + donor WGS screening, separated-pass HLA-A/B editing with matched HLA-E-only DT9 controls, per-locus phased BAF checks, and PE2max as lead TYK2 editor with PE4max held behind strict MSI clearance.

title: Passing 3D pouch oxygen on spatial averages instead of worst-face edges, sizing catalase from Day-7 retention alone, or halving dose at fixed microwell pitch
idea: Judge 3D pouch oxygenation from the average surface oxygen across all clusters, size the catalase peroxide barrier from 7-day retention alone (or let unrelated device fields skip human catalase checks), or shrink clusters from 100 µm to 80 µm at the old microwell spacing without adjusting pouch area.
why: A pouch can average over 17 mmHg across its clusters while edge faces on 100 µm clusters dip to 12.6–13.1 mmHg (or 14.3 mmHg on a 30 mmHg bead-free sheet) below the 15 mmHg insulin-secretion threshold. Catalase sized only for 70% retention at Day 7 can also fall below the 14-day 73,800 IU floor if second-week loss continues or if extra loading breaches the 158,300 U pre-cure and 0.50 EU endotoxin caps, and switching to 80 µm clusters at fixed 198.8 µm pitch halves islet dose from 1,500 to 768 IEQ per cm².
check: Require unrounded worst-face oxygen at or above 15.0 mmHg and core oxygen at or above 5.0 mmHg across both cell bands on 40, 60 and 80 meshes, enforce same-lot Day-7 (at least 70%) and Day-14 (at least 73,800 IU) human P04040 catalase retention with z = 70.0 µm peroxide at or below 2.5 µM and unrounded 0.50 EU total endotoxin on every calcium-peroxide device, and tighten 80 µm microwells to 142.22 µm square / 152.83 µm hexagonal spacing.
instead: Gate every 3D pouch on unrounded multi-mesh worst-face oxygen, bind two-timepoint human P04040 catalase and endotoxin limits directly to every calcium-peroxide assembly, and keep 1,500 IEQ per cm² dose-matched on 80 µm clusters.

title: Comparing edits across mismatched donor lines, using normal-curve shortcuts on small batch counts, or skipping imprinting, X-inactivation, 1q32.1 MDM4 and mtDNA checks
idea: Compare candidate gene edits across stem-cell lines from different people, pass six-batch release checks with large-sample normal-curve cut-offs or underpowered 6-versus-3 bank comparisons, or skip DNA imprinting, female X-chromosome silencing, late 1q32.1 MDM4 copy-number and mitochondrial DNA checks.
why: Differences between human stem-cell donors often outweigh the effect of a single gene edit, while normal-curve cut-offs inflate false passes more than twofold at six batches and 6-versus-3 bank tests miss real equivalence less than half the time. Stem-cell banking and differentiation can also select for silent 1q32.1 MDM4 or 20q11.21 BCL2L1 chromosome gains, disrupt 11p15.5 or 14q32.2 imprinted genes that govern beta-cell maturation, erode X-inactivation in female lines, or expand inherited mitochondrial DNA mutations.
check: Compare gene edits inside paired batches from the same donor line, confirm agreement across at least two unrelated blood-group O/O seedlines using six batches per bank with exact Student-t and Welch equivalence tests, and run paired bank-and-Stage-7 checks for IC1/IC2/IG-DMR methylation, 46,XX X-inactivation (at least 279 of 300 cells), 1q32.1 MDM4 and 20q11.21 copy number, and 1,000x mitochondrial DNA sequencing with respiration reserve.
instead: Block primary edit comparisons within Donor 1 (at least 6 paired batches), require 6 + 6 batches across at least two unrelated O/O banks for confirmatory equivalence, and enforce conjunctive imprinting, X-inactivation, MDM4/BCL2L1 and mitochondrial release gates.

title: Carrying prior-batch test passes onto an untested batch, releasing research-only comparators, or rounding rare-event cell counts
idea: Let a new cell batch inherit passing lab readouts or old standard errors from an earlier batch of the same cell bank, clear research-only comparators for encapsulation, or shrink rare-event cell counts by a simple recovery fraction or unverified cluster adjustment.
why: Testing a master cell bank once does not prove that a newly differentiated islet batch or assembled pouch passed potency, sterility, viral persistence or safety-switch checks, and pairing a new batch average with an old batch standard error hides measurement uncertainty. Likewise, fractional cell counts, rounded-down recovery adjustments (such as 0 in 920 cells at 32.5% recovery, whose true 95% upper bound still exceeds 1%) or unlatched safety stops can let clonal escape, persistent viral antigen or unsupported research comparators slip past release.
check: Bind every measurement to an immutable 4-, 5- or 7-part bank, batch or assembled-device identity, reject fractional or missing cell denominators, require zero observed persistent-virus or shedding events, compute exact binomial/Poisson upper bounds divided by measured recovery, and keep safety stops latched until a verified same-scope root-cause reset.
instead: Isolate batch- and device-level evidence strictly per lot and device, hold all research-only comparators out of clinical release, and enforce integer rare-event counts with latched safety stops.

title: Using DNA breaks and bacterial plasmids for large multi-gene inserts, or copying rodent adenosine rules to human islets
idea: Cut both DNA strands with Cas9 to drop in a large plasmid carrying seven genes, use standard Bxb1 landing-pad direction, or assume extracellular adenosine calms immunity without touching human insulin release.
why: Double-strand breaks with large plasmids often trap bacterial backbone DNA and select for cells with faulty p53 safety brakes. Standard Bxb1 direction inserts less cleanly than inverted attP-in-genome landing pads, dual-deaminase base editors can leave extra A-to-G changes unless fully sequenced, and human beta and alpha cells respond differently to adenosine (via ADORA1 and ADORA2A) than mouse islets.
check: Verify zero bacterial backbone DNA, exact two-copy insertion, full haplotype sequencing, human islet insulin release with an ADORA1 blocker control, and fewer than 1 in 100 million surviving proliferating cells after AP1903.
instead: Keep the landing-pad wildcard strictly on backbone-free minicircles with inverted attP-in-genome Bxb1, full haplotype sequencing and human islet adenosine checks.

title: Assuming necroptosis blockers protect beta cells and blood-vessel cells the same way, or deleting TNFRSF1A unchecked
idea: Assume blocking RIPK3 necroptosis protects beta cells directly, or knock out the TNF receptor TNFRSF1A on CXCL10-driven cells.
why: Human beta-cell models resist classical RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL necroptosis (and can show phosphorylated MLKL without dying), whereas blood-vessel cells can die by necroptosis. Meanwhile, people rarely tolerate losing TNFRSF1A, and removing it weakens the TNF signal that helps turn on the CXCL10 protective switch.
check: Measure survival and drug rescue separately in insulin-making cells and blood-vessel cells over time alongside cell-death markers.
instead: Test beta cells and blood-vessel cells separately rather than assuming one shared death pathway, and keep TNFRSF1A intact on CXCL10-driven designs.

title: Adding the CD155 Ala67Thr variant to B2M-off cells without testing natural killer cells that carry activating CD226
idea: Copy the protective CD155 (PVR) Ala67Thr variant from HLA-intact beta cells straight onto B2M-off cells to calm natural killer cells.
why: On cells that still keep their normal HLA flags, CD155 Ala67Thr reduced natural killer cell attack. On B2M-off cells with no classical HLA flags, however, CD155 can instead trigger killing through the activating receptor CD226, adds 38 non-reference peptide stretches for nearly 9 in 10 recipients, and makes the B2M repair template too large for one AAV6 virus.
check: Test sorted TIGIT-low, CD226-high natural killer cells directly against matched B2M-off stem-cell islets.
instead: Hold any CD155 engineering outside the core design unless matched B2M-off natural killer cell tests stay at or below 8% killing.

title: Relying on standalone M101 hemoglobin for 3-day oxygen, unencapsulated rest drugs, or unwashed Nec-1 conditioning
idea: Replace calcium-peroxide oxygen beads with dissolved M101 marine hemoglobin, soak hydrogels in free channel-blocking drugs to lower oxygen use, or pre-treat cells with 100 µM Nec-1 without washing.
why: In a closed 10 mL graft slab, standalone M101 holds less than 9 seconds of oxygen above 15 mmHg (about 2.2 micromoles versus 5,491 micromoles from calcium peroxide). Free channel blockers wash out of a thin hydrogel in seconds and can blunt alpha-cell glucagon rescue, while unwashed or high-dose Nec-1 carries off-target effects and can interfere with survival readouts.
check: Time oxygen depletion in a closed chamber, measure 120-hour whole-organoid oxygen use, and confirm washed cell pellets have no leftover drug and normal NQO1 enzyme activity.
instead: Keep the full 791.5 mg calcium-peroxide oxygen budget unless encapsulated slow-release depots pass 120-hour organoid and glucagon checks, and require washed low-dose Nec-1s + Ferrostatin-1 pellets.

title: Using cow or fungal catalase, bare peroxide beads next to islet cells, or unhydrolysed maleimide FasL linkers
idea: Use off-the-shelf bovine or fungal catalase in the oxygen layer, let calcium-peroxide beads sit directly against islet clusters, or attach Fas-ligand gel proteins with standard unhydrolysed maleimide linkers.
why: Cow and fungal catalases are 51% to 100% foreign to the human immune system. Bare edge beads create 7 to 19.5 µM hydrogen-peroxide plumes right beside beta cells that make almost no catalase of their own, and unhydrolysed maleimide bonds can reverse in body fluids and shed free Fas ligand (which is toxic to the liver), while pre-existing anti-PEG or repeat-dose anti-streptavidin antibodies can coat the gel.
check: Confirm human catalase (P04040) identity and low shedding, measure 24-hour burst peroxide below 2.5 µM across a 20 µm barrier film, verify at least 98% linker ring-opening by mass spectrometry, and test 72-hour human liver-cell safety.
instead: Lock the oxygen layer strictly to recombinant human catalase (P04040) inside 20 µm barrier films with wet-sieved beads of 50 µm or less, and require self-hydrolysing linkers and human-serum antibody checks.

title: Secreting soluble IL1R2 decoys alone from blood-vessel cells, or knocking out 16p13 CLEC16A, CASP8 or FADD
idea: Have nearby blood-vessel cells secrete soluble IL1R2 decoy receptors to soak up IL-1β, or knock out nearby diabetes-linked genes CLEC16A, CASP8 or FADD.
why: On the beta-cell surface, IL1R1 pairs straight away with its partner protein IL1RAcP on the same membrane, which soluble IL1R2 alone cannot outcompete without co-secreted soluble IL1RAcP. Meanwhile, at 16p13 the diabetes risk signal loops to DEXI while CLEC16A itself protects beta-cell mitochondria, and knocking out CASP8 or FADD unleashes lytic necroptosis.
check: Compare beta-cell survival under IL-1β and Fas ligand when IL1R1 and FAS are dialled down inside the beta cell versus soluble IL1R2 conditioning.
instead: Retire soluble endothelial IL1R2 decoys and test cell-intrinsic IL1R1 + FAS knockdown inside the CXCL10 cassette while keeping CLEC16A, CASP8 and FADD intact.

title: Adding the TYK2 P1104A edit to HLA-C-retaining cells without checking for a new foreign peptide, or assuming P2A scars are silent
idea: Add the protective TYK2 P1104A variant to Design B's HLA-C-retaining cells and assume recipients will ignore both it and viral P2A linker scars.
why: Changing proline 1104 to alanine turns an internal peptide (SPPTKFLEL to SAPTKFLEL) into a strong predicted binder on common HLA-C types, and over 90% of people carry normal TYK2 on both chromosomes so their T cells could see SAPTKFLEL as foreign. Likewise, porcine P2A scars have zero human T-cell test records in public databases.
check: Look for SAPTKFLEL on HLA-C by mass spectrometry and test CD8+ T cells from donors with G/G, G/C and C/C TYK2 genotypes against both islet and blood-vessel cells.
instead: Enforce a fail-closed hold on TYK2-edited HLA-C cells if either peptide presentation or T-cell priming appears, and compare scar-free 2A-free cassettes side by side.

title: Cells without HLA flags can still be attacked through the patient’s own immune cells
idea: Assume cells with no HLA flags cannot trigger memory T cells or antibodies.
why: Without HLA flags, T cells cannot see the cells directly. But the patient’s own immune cells can still pick up the graft’s debris and restart the attack.
check: Mix the patient’s immune cells with debris from flag-free islets, and look for T-cell activation and cell damage.
instead: Score the autoimmune test lower, shed less debris (small clusters, pre-built vessels) and test whether extra protection is needed.

title: A resting B2M promoter may give too little HLA-E and CD47 in the first hours
idea: Assume the natural B2M promoter gives 180,000 to 220,000 CD47 molecules per cell, as seen in cells made with a virus.
why: Resting beta cells make little B2M, so HLA-E and CD47 may be too low in the first 72 hours, when natural killer cells and macrophages attack.
check: Count CD47 and HLA-E per cell on resting and inflamed cells, then test the cells against natural killer cells and macrophages.
instead: Measure the level before relying on it. If it is too low, add a steady “on” switch such as GAPDH or AAVS1.

title: Constant, unregulated IL-10 production
idea: Make the cells produce IL-10 all the time to calm nearby T cells.
why: This is a cautious project decision rather than a proven failure. The one cited study is about mast cells in the gut, not islets. Better options exist: PD-L1 and SERPINB9.
check: Examine transplanted grafts for mast cells and other immune cells.
instead: Use PD-L1 and SERPINB9, switched on by the CXCL10 gene.

title: Switching off essential or protective genes: PTPN2, TNFAIP3, CLEC16A and other T1D gene traps
idea: Switch off PTPN2, TNFAIP3, GAD2 or nearby type 1 diabetes risk genes such as CLEC16A to avoid autoimmune attack.
why: People rarely lose these genes and stay healthy. PTPN2 and TNFAIP3 protect beta cells from dying, and GAD2 makes GABA, which keeps glucagon in check. Across 112 germline type 1 diabetes genetic regions triaged in IIP-0018, switching off is likewise ruled out for the 16p13 nearest-gene mitophagy regulator CLEC16A (where risk variants loop to inflammatory DEXI instead), protective survival and identity brakes BACH2, CTSH, SOCS1, GLIS3, DLK1 and INS, and necroptosis-restraining CASP8 and FADD.
check: Expose the cells to inflammatory signals and count cell death. Measure insulin and glucagon release.
instead: Never switch them off. Dial down downstream bystander death receptors (IL1R1 and FAS), test a protective TYK2 variant, or add SERPINB9 instead.

title: Making several base or prime edits at once
idea: Assume several base or prime edits at once are risk-free.
why: Adenine base editors caused DNA rearrangements in the cited study. The project extends that concern to making several base and prime edits at once, as an engineering precaution.
check: Scan the edited cell lines for DNA rearrangements, using optical mapping, whole-genome sequencing or CAST-seq.
instead: Keep the simple design to zero base edits, and count each extra one against the score.

title: Keeping one HLA-C gene may not calm natural killer cells
idea: Assume keeping one HLA-C gene is enough to calm all natural killer cells.
why: HLA-C is made at about a tenth of the level of HLA-A and HLA-B. Without them, one HLA-C gene may not give enough of the signal that calms natural killer cells.
check: Test natural killer cells from different donors against the resting cells.
instead: Use the B2M, HLA-E and CD47 insert, or measure the signal before relying on HLA-C.

title: Switching off RNLS: more oxygen use, and no better insulin response
idea: Assume switching off RNLS always helps, based on a mouse cell study.
why: In human cells, RNLS-off cells still released insulin poorly and used more oxygen, which hurts large clusters.
check: Compare normal and RNLS-off cells for insulin release and oxygen use, in 120 µm and 200 µm clusters.
instead: Leave it out of the simple design and compare it in small clusters.

title: Switching off G6PC2 may cause low blood sugar between meals
idea: Switch off G6PC2 in every design to remove an autoimmune target.
why: G6PC2 helps set the blood sugar level at which insulin stops. Losing it may lower blood sugar between meals. This has not been seen in grafts, so it is a precaution.
check: Drop glucose from 16.7 to 2.8 mM and time how fast insulin stops. It must stop within 3 minutes.
instead: Leave it out of the simple design unless that check passes.

title: Putting the safety switch under a promoter only mature beta cells use
idea: Control the safety switch with the G6PC2 or INS promoter, so one edit does two jobs.
why: Those promoters only work in mature beta cells. Immature or rogue cells would not make the switch and could not be destroyed.
check: Mix 10% immature stem cells into the islets, add the drug AP1903 for 72 hours and count survivors. The proposed target is fewer than 1 in 100 million cells capable of regrowth.
instead: Put the switch on both copies of a safe location (AAVS1 or GAPDH) and check it works in every cell type.

title: Switching off STAT1 or JAK1 while relying on an interferon switch
idea: Switch off STAT1 or JAK1, and use an interferon-triggered switch to turn on PD-L1 and SERPINB9.
why: With STAT1 or JAK1 (or upstream IFNGR1 and IRF1) gone, the interferon signal never arrives, so the protection never turns on.
check: Treat normal and STAT1-off cells with inflammatory signals, then count PD-L1 on each cell.
instead: Keep a second trigger (NF-κB), as the CXCL10 gene does, and avoid co-deleting TNFRSF1A alongside IL1R1.
